newsitem.title: GERMANY: German computer industry ad spending doubles.
newsitem.headline: German computer industry ad spending doubles.

text.p: The German computer and software industry doubled spending on advertising between 1993 and 1996 largely due to consumers' constant demand for information about new products, a market study has found.

Ad spending in the computer industry soared to 227 million marks in the three year period while spending on ads for software alone nearly tripled to 127 million marks during the same time frame, media marketing firm MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) said, based on new study data released last week.
"The computer market is marked by short product life cycles and sharp drops in price, which put companies under increasing pressure," MGM said in a summary of its study findings.

"Customers tend to be more price-conscious than brand-conscious, which means that promoting brands names in communication strategies is becoming Fuelling the increased expenditures on ads is the fact that the majority of computer users -- 55 percent -- say they inform themselves about the market regularly via television, leading software makers to spend 25 percent of their ad budgets on TV.
The other 45 percent of consumers get their information about computer industry products from radio or magazines, MGM said.
